subject.title: fix(gateway): prevent cross-client system-agent session takeover

question: Should an authenticated user identity, rather than a paired-device identity, remain the highest-precedence owner for non-delegated system-agent sessions across gateway clients?
rationale: This defines which separately connected clients may intentionally resume the same privileged setup/configuration session, and the repository policy treats session and auth boundaries as maintainer-sensitive compatibility and security decisions.

options.title: Keep user-first ownership
options.body: Allow authenticated users to resume their own system-agent sessions across paired devices, retaining device and connection keys only when no user identity exists.

options.title: Require device ownership
options.body: Bind ordinary system-agent sessions to the paired device even when a user identity exists, narrowing cross-client access at the cost of cross-device resume.

recommendation.title: Keep user-first ownership
recommendation.body: Allow authenticated users to resume their own system-agent sessions across paired devices, retaining device and connection keys only when no user identity exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor supplied the stated reconnect semantics and the implementation’s ownership-precedence rationale.
